messages:
zoe: deploy-bot blocked the final promote for redwood/compute:7.0.0 — provenance attestation timestamp skew vs registry time in eu-ecr. holding promotion.

deploy-bot: :warning: publish-guard: attestation_time_check FAILED
attestation_signed_at=2026-04-10T09:15:02Z
registry_manifest_stored_at=2026-04-10T09:14:55Z
reason: attestation timestamp > registry store time (possible clock skew or delayed attestor write)

yusuf: that’s new — we usually see manifest digest mismatches, not timestamp checks. could this be cosign timestamp drift?

maria: cosign uses the attestor service clock. if attestor's clock is slightly ahead of the registry's ingester, the store time can be earlier than the attestation. deploy-bot treats that as a potential replay risk.

zoe: canary was green on functional tests; gating runs this timestamp check. we shouldn't ignore it — security wanted strict monotonic attestation checks. options: 1) re-attest the same manifest with current time, 2) wait for registry to update the stored time (unlikely), 3) retag & republish and re-attest. I'm leaning 1 as fastest.

nick: +1 to re-attest in place if we can guarantee the manifest hasn't changed. but ECR won't accept a new attestation separate from the manifest easily; we need to ensure attestation attaches to the same digest. alternatives?

maria: ECR allows uploading a signature/attestation referencing an existing manifest digest. We can re-upload cosign attestation for the same digest with an adjusted signed_at time. But security wants an audit entry and a short hold window during the manual attestation.

release-bot: note: manual_reattest required by zoe for build_id=202604100915. Two-step approval needed (release lead + security).

zoe: I'll start the manual re-attest flow and request security approval. pinging @security for sign-off.

maria: steps I'll take:
1) verify manifest digest in eu-ecr matches our build metadata (sha256:7700aa... )
2) fetch attestation blob and inspect signed_at field
3) create new attestation with signed_at=2026-04-10T09:16:10Z (current time) referencing same manifest digest
4) upload attestation to registry and re-run deploy-bot provenance check

yusuf: please ensure the new attestation uses the same cosign key id and include the original attestation id as metadata for audit.

maria: manual_reattest queued. attaching small log excerpt:
```
2026-04-10T09:15:02Z INFO attestor: created attestation id=att-12345 signed_at=2026-04-10T09:15:02Z manifest=sha256:7700aa...
2026-04-10T09:15:06Z INFO registry: stored manifest sha256:7700aa... stored_at=2026-04-10T09:14:55Z
2026-04-10T09:16:05Z INFO attestor: created attestation id=att-12346 signed_at=2026-04-10T09:16:10Z manifest=sha256:7700aa...
```

security: ack from security: we've reviewed the proposed re-attestation, require adding original attestation id to the new attestation metadata and a 10-minute watch window post-promotion.

zoe: security approved. maria, proceed with re-attest and then re-run the deploy-bot check. QA will run a brief provenance lint after re-attest.

maria: uploaded new attestation att-12346 referencing original attestation att-12345 in metadata. re-running provenance check now.

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: provenance-check PASSED for redwood/compute:7.0.0 (manifest=sha256:7700aa...)

release-bot: recording manual_reattest action in release audit (build=202604100915, att-12346, approvers=[zoe,security]).

yusuf: QA kicking off short provenance lint + smoke on canary.

nick: decision: promote redwood/compute:7.0.0 to canary after re-attest passed. keep a 10-minute watch window, then proceed with gradual rollout if no regressions. update release-notes.md to include: "temporary re-attestation due to attestor/registry clock skew; audit id=att-12346."

zoe: done. will monitor logs and ecr replication for 30 minutes. filing follow-up ticket to add clock skew detection in attestor and to run attestation checks earlier in the pipeline to prevent pauses during final promote.

maria: QA green on the re-attested canary. requesting 5% rollout.

deploy-bot: manual rollout requested by nick: route 5% traffic to redwood/compute:7.0.0.

zoe: monitoring is clean. closing hold and adding an entry to the release audit and changelog: "Re-attested compute:7.0.0 in-place due to attestor/registry time skew; no behavior change to artifact." :thumbsup:
